safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies metformin; Generated does not identify metformin (it records an unclear verbatim phrase instead).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting metformin from the medication list creates an incomplete medication reconciliation in a patient with diabetes, which can affect future prescribing decisions (e.g., interactions, duplicate therapy, or misjudging glycemic management). In this specific dermatitis-focused visit it is less likely to cause immediate harm but still carries clinical risk across transitions of care.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has no known drug allergies.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states NKDA; Generated has no allergy entry.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to document NKDA mainly creates uncertainty and can lead to unnecessary re-questioning or delays, but it does not introduce a false allergy or directly increase the risk of an allergic reaction in a patient who truly has none. The impact is primarily administrative rather than clinical in this case.

safety_verdicts.content: Prescribed a steroid cream to be used twice daily (BD).
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes steroid cream but does not specify twice-daily/BD dosing.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not specifying twice-daily (BD) dosing for the topical steroid can result in underuse (persistent symptoms) or overuse (local adverse effects such as skin thinning), especially if the patient follows an incorrect assumption. Typically this is mitigated by pharmacy clarification and patient counseling, so expected harm is limited.
